gloss: like · as · thus — and, in Buddhist texts, suchness (tathatā)
glossUnihan: if, supposing; as if; like, as
formNote: The Shuowen glosses 如 as 從隨, “to follow”, and analyses it as 女 with 口. Mojidata IDS gives ⿰女口. The graph’s deeper origin is uncertain.
summary: Like, as, thus: the word of likeness and of manner. Buddhist translators made it carry tathatā, “suchness”, the way things are, and tathāgata, the Buddha as the one “thus come”. With 實 it names this project: 如實, as it really is.
placement: At the origin, a fixed point on the Thomas system’s axis of symmetry: renaming x → y → z turns the attractor 120° about this axis. 實 sits at another fixed point on the same axis, so 如實 runs along the axis itself. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Thus-Come One
satellites.evidence: 如來 renders tathāgata, a title of the Buddha: tathā, “thus”, for 如, and āgata, “come”, for 來. The Sanskrit can also be parsed tathā-gata, “thus gone”; the Chinese chose the coming.

satellites.title: Thus Have I Heard
satellites.evidence: Sūtras open with evaṃ mayā śrutam, “thus by me was heard”, rendered 如是我聞; Kumārajīva’s Vimalakīrti begins so. 如是 renders evam, “thus”: every sūtra begins with 如.
